tuner_timing.justification: To minimize latency, we are aggressively lowering scheduler granularity and latency parameters, preventing deep C-states, and enabling NAPI busy polling. This combination aims to reduce scheduling delays and wake-up times, and improve network packet processing latency.

Previous iterations demonstrated that reducing scheduler and migration-related latencies significantly improved p99 latency. This step further lowers these parameters to explore if the trend continues towards even better performance.

Continuing to exploit the low-latency scheduler parameters, I am now exploring a higher value for napi_busy_poll to further reduce network processing latency, as previous iterations showed significant improvements from aggressive tuning.
Continuing to reduce critical scheduler latency parameters and exploring a lower value for napi_busy_poll to further minimize p99 latency, building on previous improvements.

Reverting napi_busy_poll to the value from the best performing configuration (Iter 4) to re-evaluate its stability and confirm the optimal setting for minimizing latency, as recent variations have shown degraded performance.

Given that the best performance was achieved with napi_busy_poll=500 and higher values (900) showed worse results, we are exploring a lower value for napi_busy_poll to identify if further latency reduction is possible in this promising region. Other parameters are maintained at their best-performing values to isolate the effect of this change.

I've observed that napi_busy_poll=500 yielded the best result so far (61.81). To confirm this and refine the optimal value, I will slightly decrease napi_busy_poll to 450 to explore the immediate vicinity of the current best.
